title: A strict henselization triple has the same strict henselization
statement: Let R be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal m and separable residue-field closure K, let C be the strict henselization of R obtained from the filtered category of pointed etale R-algebra triples (S,q,phi) with q over m and residue embedding into K [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples]. For every such triple, put A=S_q and let A^{\mathrm{sh}} be its strict henselization with respect to the residue-field embedding phi: $\kappa(q)\to K$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism A^{\mathrm{sh}}\cong C compatible with S\to A\to A^{\mathrm{sh}} and S\to C; under it qA^{\mathrm{sh}} identifies with the maximal ideal mC, and the qA^{\mathrm{sh}}-adic completion, defined as \varprojlim_n A^{\mathrm{sh}}/(qA^{\mathrm{sh}})^n, identifies with \varprojlim_n C/(mC)^n.

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-strict-henselization-comparison to obtain the unique ring equivalence e compatible with the S-structural and K-residue maps. This is Steps 1-4 of the original route; ideal and completion transport remain to be proved.

By lem-weil-pbc-etale-triples-colimit-localization, ker(psi)=mC. The image of q under the t-cocone map lies in ker(psi), since the pointed residue map kills q. Conversely q contracts to m in R and rho factors through the t-cocone map, so mC is contained in the image of q. Hence qC=mC. Compatibility of e with S and Ideal.map_map now gives e(qD)=mC.

For each positive n, Ideal.quotientEquiv gives bijectivity of the quotient map induced by e modulo the nth power of qD. Apply lem-weil-pbc-henselization-completion-data; rewrite its target ideal using e(qD)=mC. This gives both the completion ring equivalence and the required evaluation compatibility, including n=0. Uniqueness of e follows from the first step after forgetting the ideal and completion clauses.
